state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you're watching a movie where the character is walking away from their home and then turns around to walk back. What would the negative-sloping section represent in that situation? This will help you understand how to interpret the graph of Fido's distance from his home more accurately.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so if the line is going down, that means Fido is getting closer to his home, like he's walking back towards it? But I'm confused because I thought a negative slope meant something bad was happening, like he'd stopped or something. So does the line going down just mean the distance is decreasing?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you're playing a game where you have to walk towards a target, then turn around and walk back. When you're walking back towards the starting point, your distance from the target is decreasing, right? So, just like in the game, a negative slope on the graph means the distance is getting smaller as Fido walks back towards his home.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I think I get it now! So the line going down doesn't mean something bad is happening - it just means the distance number is getting smaller because Fido is walking back towards home. But wait, what about the flat bit in the middle of the graph - does that mean Fido is standing still, or is he doing something else?

score.justification_pass1: While the teacher provides mathematically correct analogies and the student does show improvement in understanding that negative slope means decreasing distance (not rest), the teacher never directly addresses the core misconception about rest versus movement, and the analogies tell rather than elicit reasoning from the student.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently grounds the abstract graph interpretation in concrete, relatable scenarios (watching a movie of someone walking, playing a game where you walk toward and away from a target), making this a textbook example of the experiential strategy.
